bullets: The Macros button on each printer tile is now a full Control panel. Alongside your macros it brings heater targets and motion controls - homing, jogging, extrude and retract - into one sheet, arranged the way you want: reorder, rename and recolour the temperature, motion and macro sections, or start from the Essential, Motion or Macros presets. Any Klipper macro can become a labelled button with its own icon, colour and parameters, the parameters it needs are suggested from the macro itself, and the exact command is shown for you to review before it runs. It all saves per printer and travels in your backups.

The config editor now understands Klipper. Editing printer.cfg suggests the right section and option names as you type, warns about values that don't look right before you save, and lets you edit a macro's G-code inline. The console gained command completions to match.

The File System 'Hide backups & hidden files' filter now also catches timestamped config backups that other tools leave behind (like crowsnest's crowsnest.conf.2024-12-22-1121), and those files now open as text so you can read them.
The preheat sheet now fills the full width in landscape instead of floating in a narrow strip down the middle of the screen.

The File System browser can now hide the clutter. A checkbox at the top - ticked by default and remembered - hides Klipper's automatic SAVE_CONFIG snapshots (the printer-20260830_101530.cfg pile), .bak backup files and hidden dotfiles like .theme, so the list shows just your real config files; a folder whose entire contents are hidden disappears with them. Untick it and everything is back. The choice travels in your backups too.

Settings backups now provably carry every setting. An audit found the global power button toggle was always meant to travel in backups but never did - fixed - and an automated check now guarantees every future setting either rides your backup or has a written reason it can't (like the app lock and its PIN, which must never leave the device).

The guided tour is fixed and extended. It could point at things that were off the bottom of the screen (and you can't scroll while it runs), and in the worst case a step could strand you with no Next or Skip at all. The dashboard now jumps to the top when the tour starts, every step scrolls its target into view, and the explanation card always appears even if a highlight can't - so the tour can never get stuck again. The first tile is also always shown as a healthy, connected example printer for the whole tour, even if your real printer is offline.
The tour gains a step for the new tools: Console and File System get introduced right after the emergency stop.

Every printer tile gains two tools under its temperatures: Console and File System. Console opens the printer's G-code console as an overlay - recent history already loaded, live updates while open, errors in red, quick-command chips (they fill the input, never send by themselves), and tapping a past command puts it back in the input. It stays available mid-print and while Klipper is in an error state - exactly when you need it. File System browses the printer's config folder and opens printer.cfg (and friends) in a structured editor: setting names stay fixed, you edit only the values, and comments and layout survive a save untouched. Before your first change a backup copy is saved on the printer; Save and restart brings Klipper up on the new config and, if it fails to start, offers one-tap restore from that backup. Both work on your WiFi and over the tunnel alike, and the buttons shrink to icons on narrow tiles. Thanks to the user request behind it.

Android catches up with iPhone on loud printer alerts: a paused print (filament runout included), a failed print with Klipper's reason, and a printer error even between prints now raise heads-up notifications on their own 'Printer alerts' channel, silenceable separately from the rest. Needs Print notifications switched on in the menu.

The plugin-update badge now nudges for plugin 0.6.25, catching up three plugin releases that shipped since the last app update: 0.6.23 adds a tunnel watchdog (a dropped remote tunnel heals itself, with a strict budget so it can never flap) and the MOONGATE_STATUS console macro that diagnoses your Moongate setup from the printer; 0.6.24 makes the update button honest on installs Moonraker doesn't manage; 0.6.25 adds printer-error, pause and custom MOONGATE_NOTIFY push notifications on iPhone. And when a hand-installed plugin can't self-update, the update dialog now says to re-copy the plugin file instead of pointing at a Software Updates entry that doesn't exist.

Cameras recover instead of dying quietly. A custom camera address that stops answering falls back to the printer's own camera with a visible notice (and an amber dot on the camera gear while the override is set aside); a webcam entry left pointing at a dismantled camera service falls back to the printer's default snapshot path the same way; and a printer whose plugin is too old to serve its camera says so instead of looking broken.

iPhone fixes: opening a printer's page for the very first time no longer fails when the printer was discovered by its hostname (the voron24.local style answer iPhones often store) - the app resolves it to a usable address first, and existing installs heal on the next discovery. Moongate now requires iOS 15 or newer.
Also: Moongate now consistently describes itself as free and source available, and the usual dependency updates.

Compact tiles get the full set of quick actions. A tile with its webcam hidden used to lose every button the full tile offers: no pause or stop, no file browser, no macros, and no light control, because all of those lived on or around the camera square. The same action row the full tile shows beneath its camera now sits at the top of each compact tile, with the printer's status or live print progress on the left and the buttons on the right, including the light toggle for printers with lighting configured. Mid-print a compact tile can now pause, resume or cancel the job directly, and a printer in an error state offers its firmware-restart button, exactly like the full tile.

The plugin-update badge catches up to plugin 0.6.22. The multi-camera plugin shipped alongside v0.9.59, but no app build knew it existed yet, so tiles never nudged for it. This update teaches the badge that 0.6.22 is current: printers still on an older plugin show the amber badge again, with the usual one-tap update on plugins 0.6.16 and newer. If your printers already run 0.6.22, nothing changes.

Printers with more than one camera can now switch between them in the app. When a printer reports two or more webcams, a switch button appears on its tile's camera; tap it to pick which camera to show, on the tile and in the full-screen view alike. The choice is remembered for each printer and travels in your backups. Cameras themselves are still added, named, enabled and ordered in Mainsail or Fluidd; the app simply follows that list. Needs plugin 0.6.22 or newer on the printer (Mainsail -> Software Updates); on an older plugin the app keeps showing the first camera exactly as before, and a camera set by hand with the tile's gear always wins over the picker. Thanks to the field report that asked for it.

Tap-to-pair. The pairing page (the URL MOONGATE_PAIR prints) shows a tappable link under its QR code, for when you've opened that page on the very phone the app is on and can't scan the screen you're looking at. The app now answers that tap, on Android and iPhone alike: tapping the link opens Moongate straight into pairing, exactly as if the QR had been scanned, whether the app was already running or not.

Webcam tiles now tell you when a camera can't be reached instead of spinning forever. If a camera's address is wrong, or the camera is off, the waking spinner used to restart endlessly and look like it was forever about to connect. After a few outright connection failures the tile now says "Camera unreachable, check its address" (in all 9 languages), so a typo'd address or a powered-down camera is obvious at a glance. Fix the address or the camera and the picture comes back as before. Thanks to the field report that caught it.

Fixed printers on your own WiFi being stuck on the tunnel. On some phones, local network discovery could answer with a link-local IPv6 address (fe80::...) that apps can't actually connect to - and because a freshly discovered address is trusted over the saved one, storing it quietly broke the direct local connection for a printer sitting on the same network. Unusable addresses are now rejected before they're ever stored, so discovery can no longer poison the local path.

The printer page no longer sticks on the tunnel while you're at home (a user report: the dashboard tile said Local while the printer screen said Tunnel). The page is kept warm so re-opening it is instant, but its local-or-tunnel choice was made only once, usually when the app started - so a page first loaded away from home (or before WiFi was up) rode the tunnel forever. Opening a printer now checks the dashboard's live connection first: if your phone can currently reach the printer directly, a tunnel-riding page is rebuilt on the local network on the spot - faster Mainsail, and local-only cameras work. The refresh button always did this by hand; now it happens by itself.

The dashboard's time-remaining readout now matches Mainsail (a user report, with side-by-side screenshots: Mainsail said ~3h left while the tile said ~4h). Early in a print the old estimate extrapolated purely from elapsed time versus progress, and a print's opening minutes (brim, slow solid bottom layers) made that far too pessimistic. The app now blends the same three estimates Mainsail averages - elapsed-based, filament-used-based and the slicer's own estimate for the file - using data it already had, so the tile and the notification land within a minute or two of Mainsail's ETA. Bonus: the readout now appears in the first seconds of a print instead of hiding until 2%.

Webcam tiles are honest while a camera wakes up. A sleeping camera (typically go2rtc) can take a moment to produce its first frame; the tile used to sit blank or flash a broken image while that happened. It now shows a small wake-up spinner until the picture arrives, and only settles to the placeholder when the camera genuinely won't answer. In-app bug reports also record what each camera fetch actually returned, so camera issues can be diagnosed straight from a report.

Direct (LAN/VPN) mode now keeps its zero-cloud promise to the letter. A background session-refresh timer (and the page pre-warm at app start) could still fire pointless cloud calls for a Direct printer every few minutes - no data left your network that mattered, but it was against the promise and it cluttered the server logs. Direct printers are now excluded at every level, and the server refuses such requests outright as a second line of defence.

Optional Pi plugin update (0.6.18): the plugin's external-camera relay now logs every non-picture outcome (camera busy, timeout, connection refused) to Moonraker's log, so remote-camera issues can be pinned down from the printer's log alone. No behaviour change - updating is optional and there's deliberately no update badge for it.
Also: three package updates (the QR scanner and the two web-view packages).

Fixes the v0.9.54 dashboard: every tile could sit stuck on 'Connecting...' forever even though the printers were fine (opening a printer's page still worked). The v0.9.54 anti-flicker change accidentally stopped every status update from reaching the tiles. If your dashboard went quiet after updating, this brings it straight back - sorry about that one.

iPhone only: the stray empty strip at the bottom of the dashboard is gone. v0.9.54's 'keep clear of the system bars' padding was meant for Android's button bar and now applies only there - iPhones have no button bar, so the tiles and the embedded printer page fill the screen again.
iPhone only: the add and reorder buttons now sit planted in the bottom corners, the same as on Android, instead of floating well above the screen edge.

Moongate now runs on 3rd-party printers. Machines that were never a Raspberry Pi - first up, the Elegoo Centauri Carbon on OpenCentauri COSMOS firmware - can join the dashboard in Direct (LAN/VPN) mode with a one-file install: the Pi plugin no longer needs any extra Python packages in LAN-only mode. A new '3rd-party printer support' guide on GitHub has the steps, validated on a real Centauri.

Nothing hides under your phone's buttons any more. The dashboard's last tile (its name and temperatures could sit under the Android navigation bar), the bottom of the embedded Mainsail/Fluidd page, the pairing form and the notification settings list all now stay clear of the system bars - on iPhone too.

A steadier dashboard on flaky WiFi. A sub-second network blip used to blank a tile's webcam and temperatures for a few seconds and could shuffle the tile order (with auto-arrange on). The app now waits for a second failed check before believing a printer has gone offline, so blips are invisible while a genuinely unplugged printer still shows offline within seconds.

See when a print will finish, right on the dashboard (a user request). While a printer is printing, its tile now shows a small time readout after the temperatures: how long is left (~1h09m). It uses the same estimate as the print notification, so the two always agree, and it works on every printer without updating the Pi plugin.

Prefer a finish time instead? In menu → Dashboard layout you can switch the readout to show the projected finish time (15:27, in your 12/24-hour clock format) rather than the time left - or hide it entirely with the new 'Show time remaining' switch. Your choice is saved and travels in backups.
The readout appears a couple of minutes into a print (too early, the estimate would be nonsense) and hides while paused, since a paused print's estimate can't be trusted.

go2rtc webcams now show up. If your camera runs through go2rtc (a stream.html address in Mainsail's webcam settings, e.g. WebRTC mode), the dashboard tile and the full-screen camera now display it: the app spots the go2rtc address and quietly asks go2rtc for plain snapshots of the same source, so it renders like any other camera - reverse-proxy paths and non-standard ports included. Works whether the camera was auto-detected from Mainsail or pasted into a tile's gear as a custom URL.

Live video now plays inside the printer page. Mainsail shows go2rtc cameras as an auto-playing video, and phones block auto-playing video by default - so the camera card sat black in the app while working fine on a PC. The app's built-in printer page now allows it, on Android and iPhone.

Sturdier camera tiles: a camera address that answers with something that isn't a picture (a web page, an error page) no longer paints a broken image over the tile - the placeholder simply stays until real frames arrive.

Honest limitation: a camera on a public web address still can't ride the Moongate cloud tunnel when you're away - the Pi's camera relay deliberately talks only to devices on your home network (a security guard). On home WiFi, in Direct (LAN/VPN) mode, or over your own VPN it all works.

Run it your way: a new Direct (LAN/VPN) mode adds a printer with zero cloud. Install the Pi plugin in LAN-only mode, pick 'Direct (LAN/VPN)' at the top of the Add Printer screen, then scan its QR or type its address - the app talks straight to Moonraker on your network, nothing touches the internet, and it keeps working with no internet at all. Away from home you connect through your own VPN (WireGuard, Tailscale). Honest trade-offs, shown right on the screen: no print notifications in Direct mode, remote access is your VPN's job, your phone's network must be in Moonraker's trusted_clients, and give the Pi a fixed address.

Switch an existing printer between cloud and Direct any time from its edit dialog (the pencil on the printer page) - no re-pairing, takes effect straight away. And if you later cloud-pair a machine you'd added as Direct, the app absorbs the old tile automatically, keeping its settings.

Printers now need a real name: the name box starts empty and cycles example names ('Voron 2.4', 'RatRig 300', 'Wilma'...), and adding without one shows a friendly reminder. No more dashboards full of 'My Printer'.
The plugin update icon has moved to the bottom-left corner of the camera box, next to the power button (it was top-right among the camera controls).

The dashboard now tells you when a printer's Moongate plugin is out of date: a small amber update icon appears on that machine's camera box (or next to the power button on compact tiles) and stays until the plugin is updated - it disappears by itself the moment the printer reports the new version.

Tap the icon and, on plugins from 0.6.16 onward, one tap updates the plugin straight from your phone - the printer fetches and applies it in the background. Older plugins get pointed at Mainsail's Software Updates panel instead (they predate the one-tap path; after this update they have it). Machines that are mid-print are left alone until the print finishes.
Not app-only: update the Moongate plugin (0.6.16) from Moonraker's update panel to give your printers the one-tap update path.

The "How pairing works" pop-up finally stops re-appearing on every launch: its "Don't show this again" tick was hiding at the bottom of the scrolling text where most phones never showed it - it now sits right above the OK button. The notice also now tells you the one thing to do after installing the plugin: run the MOONGATE_PAIR macro on the printer (or type it in the Mainsail/Fluidd console) to get your pairing code or QR link.

Starred macros no longer vanish. Starring a macro, closing the macro menu and opening it again could silently drop the new stars (they only came back after restarting the app) - the menu now always shows your latest stars.

Printers removed from your account stop calling home. The Pi plugin used to keep checking in every 5 minutes forever after its printer was removed; it now notices, goes quiet, and leaves a note in the Klipper console - pairing again wakes it instantly.
Not app-only: this release also updates the Moongate Pi plugin (0.6.15) with the go-quiet fix above - update the plugin from Moonraker's update panel too.

Hold your finger on a tile's camera picture and it opens full screen - the same pinch-to-zoom live view as the little eye icon, running at your camera's full frame rate. Close it and the dashboard tiles go straight back to your chosen feed rate.

New: a Local only switch. Turn on the Local-only button in the menu and a cloud icon appears in the top bar - tap it and Moongate stops using the remote tunnel entirely, connecting only to printers on your own network (everything else shows offline until you tap it again). Handy if you only ever print from home, and it stops all remote checking in the background too.

The Local camera feed rate now defaults to Raw (your camera's own frame rate) - Wi-Fi can afford it. If you ever picked a rate yourself your choice is kept, and the mobile-data rate stays throttled at 3s.

Print cards get their own notification category again, separate from the all-printers status bar, so you can silence one without the other. A new row under Print notifications jumps straight to your phone's per-category switches.
Opening a printer whose Pi is still starting up no longer shows a raw "Bad gateway" error page: Moongate now explains it in plain English and retries by itself until the web interface comes up.

Fixed: a printer that no longer exists on your account (deleted, or moved to another phone by a restore) made the app silently re-check it every few seconds forever. It now backs off, saving your battery and data.

Not app-only: this release also updates the Moongate Pi plugin (0.6.13) with a fix that stops a Pi that can't load its signing keys from retrying on every request - update the plugin from Moonraker's update panel too.
New language: Brazilian Portuguese! A full translation contributed by community member Daniel Morais (obrigado!), making nine languages. Pick it on first launch or any time from the menu.

Restoring a backup now keeps any printers you paired after that backup was made, adding the backup's printers alongside them. If you'd rather the dashboard match the backup exactly, the restore asks and offers that as a choice, and cancelling changes nothing and doesn't use up the backup's one-time restore code.

The per-print notification now shows heat from the very first moments: the warm-up climb (like 25→220°) while heaters ramp, then your chosen hotend and bed readings. Progress and time estimates still join a little later, once the print is far enough along for them to be trustworthy.
Filled in missing translations: the Delete-my-data screens now show in your language instead of English.
App-only update, no Pi update needed.

New: a pause / play button in the dashboard top bar to quickly turn print notifications off and on. When your printers will be off for a while, tap pause to stop Moongate checking on them in the background and save battery, then tap play to start watching again. It only shows when notifications are on, and a pause is remembered even if you restart the app.
App-only update, no Pi update needed.

Fixed: a printer switched back on while Moongate was in the background could stay stuck on "offline" until you force-closed and reopened it. Moongate now re-checks each printer's live status the moment you return to the app.

Multi-toolhead preheat now sends each hotend its own command, so setting several tools at once is more reliable and one heater refusing a target no longer stops the others. The preheat panel also scrolls, so every tool fits on a tool changer with lots of hotends.

Multi-toolhead detection, fixed at the source: the printer now sends every hotend and the active tool to the app in one go, so all your tools show on the dashboard even over a remote or VPN connection where the app couldn't fetch them separately before.
This one is not app-only: update the Moongate plugin on your printer too, from Moonraker's update panel (Machine tab), so it sends the extra hotends. Single-hotend and IDEX printers are unaffected.

More reliable multi-toolhead detection: tool changers (klipper-toolchanger / StealthChanger) are now recognised straight from the printer's tool setup, reading each tool's own hotend and the active tool, so every hotend shows on the dashboard. Plain single-hotend and IDEX printers are detected exactly as before.
App-only update, no Pi update needed.

Multi-toolhead preheat: long-press the temperatures on a tool changer or IDEX printer and the Preheat sheet now lists every hotend (T0, T1, T2 and so on) as its own row, so you can set them all at once, plus the bed. Single-hotend printers look exactly as before.

Multi-toolhead notifications: the print notification's hotend reading now shows every tool's temperature on one line (for example 210° 205° 25°) instead of just the first tool. Single-hotend printers still show the one reading.

Fixed: the "Printer unreachable" screen (shown when a printer can't be reached over the tunnel) now fills the whole page in your theme, instead of leaving a blank strip down the side with the failed page showing through.
App-only update, no Pi update needed.

New: a "Show dashboard buttons" switch (menu -> Dashboard Layout). Turn it off to hide the add and reorder buttons that float at the bottom of the dashboard - handy when you have a lot of printers and the buttons cover the bottom tiles. You can still add a printer from the menu, and turn the switch back on when you want to reorder.
App-only update, no Pi update needed.

The dashboard temperatures now stay one consistent size on every tile, set only by the display-size slider. Instead of shrinking to tiny text when a tile is busy or narrow (a regression from the v0.9.39 font update), they wrap onto another row, or stack the icon above the number, to fit.

Multi-toolhead printers use the tile width better: on a wide single-column tile all the tool temperatures sit on one line with the bed and chamber, and they only flow onto extra rows when the tile is narrow.
App-only update, no Pi update needed.

New: printers with more than one toolhead (IDEX and tool changers) now show every hotend on the dashboard tile. Each tool gets its own temperature labelled T0, T1, T2 and so on, the tool currently in use is highlighted, and the bed and chamber move to a row beneath. Single-toolhead printers look exactly as before.

The font picker now has a lot more to choose from - over 30 typefaces grouped by style (sans, rounded, serif, slab, monospace, techy, condensed, handwriting and even retro/pixel), each previewed in its own font.
Tight spots like printer names and the temperature row now auto-shrink so no font ever gets clipped, whichever one you pick.

Fixed: the persistent status notification now follows your dashboard order. With "Auto-arrange by status" turned off (so your printers stay in the order you arranged them), the notification lists them the same way, instead of always floating the busiest printer to the top.
App-only update, no Pi update needed.

New: choose the app's font. A Font option in the menu (under Theme) switches the whole app between a Default, Rounded, Serif, and High-readability typeface. Apps can't read the specific font you've set in your phone's own settings, so this is a small built-in set instead. Your choice is saved and travels in backups.
Tutorial polish: in the temperatures step, the hotend, bed and chamber readings are now highlighted inside one box together, rather than a separate ring around each.
App-only update, no Pi update needed.

New: a "Phone colours" theme. On Android 12 and newer, choose Phone colours in the menu and Moongate matches your phone's own colour scheme - the wallpaper-based palette Android calls Material You - and follows your light/dark setting automatically. It sits alongside Dark, Light and Custom, and only appears on phones that support it (older Android and iPhone have no system palette to read, so it stays hidden there).

The first-run tutorial is a little shorter: the hotend, bed and chamber temperatures are now introduced together in one step instead of three, it skips the menu items that explain themselves - Theme, About, Settings and Buy me a coffee - and the button to leave the tour early reads "End" instead of "Skip".
App-only update, no Pi update needed.

New: an optional in-app tutorial. After you add your first printer, Moongate offers a quick guided walkthrough that highlights each part of the app live - the green/orange connection bars and what they mean, the tunnel-still-building marker, the hotend, bed and chamber temperatures, the double-tap emergency stop, the webcam, and preheat - then opens the menu and walks every option in it. Move through it with Next and Back, leave with Skip, and run it again any time from the bottom of the menu.
The press-and-hold area that opens preheat is now the whole tile (name and temperatures), so it's much easier to trigger - it had become fiddly at larger display sizes.
Delete my data now lives in Settings alongside Remove all printers, instead of its own menu entry.

The display-size slider in the menu (renamed from "Font size") now scales the dashboard icons as well as the text, so the whole dashboard grows and shrinks together. The emergency-stop button resizes with it and is a little smaller by default.
At larger display sizes, each printer's hotend, bed and chamber temperatures now stack into two rows (icons above the values) so they no longer run off the edge of a narrow tile.

New first-run reminder at the top of "How pairing works": it points out that the Moongate plugin must be installed on your printer's Pi first, with a one-tap link to the setup guide. It keeps the usual "don't show again".
Plus a round of text and styling tidy-ups across the app.

Power all machines now works with printers powered by a Klipper macro (the Advanced Power Switch), not only smart-plug power devices. It also reads how each printer is set up and shows the right buttons, so a machine can be off only, on only, or both.
Advanced Power Switch now lets you set just a Power Off macro (the common case), without forcing a Power On macro too. A single toggle macro keeps working from the tile's own power button.
After an in-app update installs, the downloaded file is cleared from the cache, so the app no longer holds on to that extra storage.

New: an optional Global power button in the top bar. Turn it on under the menu and it adds a button that opens a "power all machines" sheet. Switch every machine's power on with a tap, or off with a deliberate slide-to-confirm. Machines that are printing are left on, unreachable ones are skipped, and the sheet shows exactly which machines will switch before you commit
It is off by default, and only useful if your machines have a Moonraker power device (a smart plug or relay) set up

Pi plugin fix (a separate, optional update): a printer that had lost its pairing used to retry every few seconds forever in the background. It now backs off to the normal interval, which cuts wasted battery, data and cloud load. Get it from Moonraker's update panel. The app feature itself needs no Pi update

Fixed: the chamber temperature could be missing from the dashboard for some setups, in particular a combined chamber sensor (several probes averaged into one reading) or one whose name uses capital letters, and especially when connecting remotely over the tunnel. Moongate now finds the chamber reliably in those cases

Print notifications: when "Show only online devices" is on and every printer is currently offline, the ongoing notification now reads "Watching your printers" instead of "No printers online", which looked like an error
No Pi update needed, just update the app

Fixed the "Show only online devices" toggle (added in v0.9.29) resetting itself to off every time you reopened the app. It saved your choice but didn't read it back when the app started, so the switch always looked off - and if your printers were offline you could be left with a "no printers online" notification that was hard to clear, because the switch showed off while the setting was actually still on. The toggle now remembers its setting and shows the right state when you reopen the app
No Pi update needed - just update the app

New: long-press a printer's hotend/bed temperatures on its tile (while it's online and idle) to open a Preheat panel - set a hotend and/or bed temperature and tap Set to send it straight to that machine. Leave either box empty to heat just one (e.g. the hotend for a filament change, or the bed to warm up before a print)

Optional heat-soak timer: enter a number of minutes and you'll get a notification when it's up, so you know the machine has fully warmed through before you start a print. 0 means no timer - it just sets the temperatures
Works whether your config names the heaters extruder/heater_bed or something custom - Moongate detects the right names from the printer
The heat-soak alert rides the print-notification service, so it needs Print notifications switched on - the panel flags that (with a one-tap toggle) if they're off
No Pi update needed - just update the app

New: "Show only online devices" - a toggle under Print notifications. Turn it on and the ongoing status notification lists only your online printers; machines that are offline or switched off drop off the list, so it isn't cluttered with printers you're not using. Turn it off to see them all again
No Pi update needed - just update the app

Fixed the status notification showing a printer as "Printing" after you'd switched it off. On machines that keep the Raspberry Pi powered when the printer's mainboard is off (e.g. a separate Pi supply), the printer now correctly shows as Offline and any stuck "printing" card is cleared
No Pi update needed - just update the app
Print notifications no longer swap places in the shade - the live card for a running print now stays pinned directly beneath the status notification, instead of jumping above it

To keep them together the print card now shares the status notification's quiet channel: a print starting or finishing no longer buzzes or pops up - the card simply appears, quietly, under the status list and updates there
No Pi update needed - just update the app

The Update button in the in-app "What's new" pop-up now installs the update inside the app - downloading the new version with a progress bar and launching the installer - instead of opening the browser to GitHub. It now matches the Update button on the update banner, and a "View on GitHub" option is still there if you'd rather download it manually

The live print notification no longer needs to be expanded to read - the progress bar is gone, so the print details (progress, time remaining, finish time, temperatures) now sit on the notification itself, visible at a glance without pulling it open
No Pi update needed - just update the app
Reworked print notifications. The ongoing notification is now a clean status list - every printer with just its state (Printing / Ready / Idle / Offline), no progress numbers or temperatures
Each active print now gets its own separate notification with live progress, time remaining and the projected finish time; it appears when the print starts and updates as it runs

When a print finishes, its card shows the finish time and can be cleared - swipe it away or tap Clear and the print is reset on the printer too, so the dashboard's Done badge and the status list go back to Ready together. Clearing it from the dashboard removes the card as well
The separate pop-up alerts are gone - the card is the single surface, buzzing once when a print starts and once when it finishes
Choose what each print card shows under Print notifications → Notification content (progress, time remaining, finish time, hotend, bed)
No Pi update needed - just update the app

Printer tiles now show just the current temperature for the hotend, bed and chamber - the target reading (the “/265°” shown after the current “265°”) no longer appears on the tile. During a print that extra text had been widening the temperature row enough to push the Emergency-stop button off the edge of the tile; the row now stays compact and the E-STOP stays put. The heater icon still turns its accent colour while it's heating, and the live print notification still shows the target
No Pi update needed - just update the app

Emergency stop from the dashboard. Each online printer tile now shows a small red warning triangle (beside the temperature readout) - double-tap it to send an immediate emergency stop (Klipper M112). It's a double-tap with no confirmation so a single stray tap can't trigger it; once stopped, the triangle turns into a restart button - tap it to firmware-restart and bring the machine back online (manual, not automatic, so you can check the cause first)

In-app updates with a progress bar. When a new version is available, tapping Update now downloads it inside Moongate (with a progress bar) and opens the installer for you, instead of bouncing you out to the browser. Android still shows its standard install confirmation

Powered-off printers no longer cost anything in the background - the app (the dashboard and the print-notification service alike) detects they're offline from the cloud and stops requesting access for them, instead of pinging every few seconds. Less mobile data and battery, and offline tiles settle faster
No Pi update needed - just update the app

Camera feeds are now smarter about your connection - the faster 'Local' refresh rate is used whenever your phone is on Wi-Fi, even when you're away from home and reaching a printer through the tunnel. The slower 'Tunnel' rate now only kicks in on mobile data, where it actually saves you data

Printers warm up in the background the moment you open the app, so the first time you tap a printer it opens instantly instead of showing Mainsail's 'Initializing…' - the same instant open as before, now ready from the very first tap

Lighter on mobile data and battery - the app and the background notification service now reuse a cached connection token instead of re-requesting one every few seconds, and no longer keep requesting tokens for printers that are switched off
No Pi update needed - just update the app

Separate camera feed rates for home and away - a new 'Dashboard Camera Feeds' screen in the menu lets you set the tile webcam refresh rate independently for your local (WiFi) connection and the remote (tunnel) connection
Each tile automatically uses the local rate at home and the tunnel rate when you're away, so you can keep a fast feed on WiFi and a slower one over mobile data to save bandwidth
New tunnel feeds default to 3s (a data saver); your existing setting carries over to both. No Pi update needed - just update the app

Drag your printer tiles into any order again - turn off 'Auto-arrange by status' in the menu, tap the drag-drop button (bottom-left), then drag the tiles around the dashboard (both full and compact tiles) and tap the green check to finish. The tidy masonry layout returns as soon as you're done
Restoring a backup now rebuilds your dashboard to match it exactly - the same printer order and each tile's layout (including which webcams are hidden), not just adding any missing printers

If the phone already has printers that aren't in the backup, restore asks before removing them (and lists them first), so you can't lose a printer you paired after making the backup. On a fresh phone there's nothing to remove, so it just restores

Show or hide each printer's webcam - the menu's Webcams entry opens a list of your printers, each with a switch. A hidden webcam also stops that tile fetching its camera, so it doubles as a per-printer data saver - this replaces the old all-or-nothing 'Show webcams' switch with per-printer control
See-through tiles - on the Custom theme you can now set a tile opacity (0-100) so your dashboard background shows through the tiles, while the camera feed stays solid

Clear a finished print right from the tile - when a job ends, its tile shows a Done (or Cancelled) badge; tap the small × on it to send the printer back to Idle. One tap, no pop-up, and your print notification updates to Idle too

Give the dashboard your own background - switch to the Custom theme, open it from the menu, then pick any image from your phone to sit behind the tiles. Advanced Power Switch (in the menu, beside Lighting) - for printers whose power is a Klipper macro instead of a Moonraker power device: set an On + Off pair or a single toggle macro, and the tile's power button drives the printer through it. Drag them into any order you like and switch off the ones you don't care about - want only the finish time and not the running time? Turn it off. A live preview updates as you tweak, and your choices are saved and travel in your backups
